Sports.title: Bellamy 'hurting' after Denmark beat Wales comfortably
Sports.content:
Craig Bellamy says he is “really hurting” after Wales were beaten 2-0 in Copenhagen by a dominant Denmark to leave them bottom of their Nations League group

Both of Denmark's goals came from set pieces delivered by Brentford midfielder Mikkel Damsgaard with Ben Davies turning into his own net shortly after the break before Gustav Iskasen's deflected strike put the game beyond doubt.

Wales were second best throughout and could have been behind in the first half with Damsgaard striking the post from range moments after Isaksen had a volley ruled out by VAR for a marginal offside from Rasmus Hojlund in the build-up.

Craig Bellamy's depleted side battled to a 1-0 defeat against Portugal in Lisbon on Thursday but they were utterly outclassed by Denmark in Copenhagen in a result that paints a bleak picture for their hopes in Nations League Group A4.

Wales have failed to register a single goal or point in their first two games and they face an uphill battle if they are to avoid relegation from this group.

Denmark were under similar pressure after being beaten by Norway on Thursday, and there was turmoil in the camp after captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg openly questioned the team's tactics, but they rose to the occasion and could easily have won more comfortably.

The only negative for Denmark was an injury to Manchester United's Patrick Dorgu, who was forced off after 30 minutes and headed straight down the tunnel.

Wales have no let up as they face Norway and Erling Haaland on Thursday in their third Nations League match. Norway were beaten 2-1 by Portugal in Oslo later on Sunday.

Key moments from Copenhagen

24: DENMARK GOAL RULED OUT BY VAR! Isaksen's volley is chalked off for a marginal offside on Hojlund.

27: OFF THE POST! Damsgaard rattles a shot off the frame of the goal for Denmark.

30: INJURY! Dorgu forced off with an apparent injury problem.

43: VITAL SAVE! Filip Jorgensen produces a big hand to keep out Connor Roberts' close-range effort.

53: GOAL! Denmark lead through a Davies own-goal after Damsgaard's free-kick.

66: GOAL! Denmark double their lead through Isaksen's deflected strike at another set piece.

Bellamy: It will be a tough watch back

Wales boss Craig Bellamy:

"I'm really hurting. When you see an athletic team run over you a little bit… but then, will we improve? I think we will.

"This team will get better, these players will keep improving. There are young ones coming in well after I'm gone.

"For me now it's just focus, two more games to go. How can I help you improve for the next two games, but also how can I improve?

"I'm probably more loving when I'm losing, I'm probably more of a pain in the backside when I'm winning.

"I said to the players before the game, 'this is going to be tougher than Portugal'. It was a different challenge, but a very difficult one. The best team won overall.

"As disappointed as I am with that, the result I probably think was fair. We move on. It will be a tough watch back.

"How the players put their bodies on the line was brilliant. They are really special for that. I really admire that, but I want more."

Ampadu: Disappointing night for Wales

Wales midfielder Ethan Ampadu to BBC Sport:

"Disappointing night for us. Always going to be difficult against a top team away from home. But we didn't really put in our levels. We gave everything we could.

"We could have been tidier on the ball, especially in transitions. We didn't create enough to score today.

"Frustrating to concede [both goals from set pieces]. We pride ourselves on being difficult to beat on set pieces and work so hard on it. We just didn't defend well enough today at set pieces."

Sports.title: Hearn: Fury vs AJ press conference not 'confirmed'
Sports.content:
With so much uncertainty around the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight, even their first press conference has been thrown into doubt.

Fury and Joshua have a rivalry that's been more than a decade in the making. This week the fight was finally set for December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, but within 48 hours of it being announced a promotional dispute erupted leading to mounting speculation that the mega-fight could be called off.

Fury and Joshua's first head-to-head press conference was due to take place on Wednesday. But that may not go ahead now.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn told Sky Sports: "At the moment nothing confirmed for next week press conference wise."

As to whether Fury could hold one without Joshua and Hearn, the Matchroom promoter said: "With regards to are we expecting to be there, there wouldn't be one without us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dillian Whyte believes that rumours the fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could fall through is nothing more than mind games - and gives his prediction for the fight

The announcement for the long-awaited Fury-AJ fight stated that Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and Dana White were staging the bout, although Hearn has publicly claimed the American promoter cannot be involved.

Speaking after Johnny Fisher's victory over Michael Pirotton on Saturday night, White revealed he was uncertain whether the Fury-AJ fight itself would still go ahead. As to whether Wednesday's press conference would happen, White said: "I have no idea."

He also didn't confirm whether he'd be in attendance himself. "I guess I'll leave that as a surprise," White said.

Sports.title: Medina stars for Man Utd, Liverpool end Anfield hoodoo, Arsenal's title hopes over?
Sports.content:
Are Arsenal's title chances over already?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the WSL match between Chelsea and Arsenal at Stamford Bridge

It seems a touch early to definitely say whether or not Arsenal's title chances are over already, but their start has left a lot to be desired.

Four games in, they have scored only twice and one of those goals - in the 1-1 draw with Man Utd last weekend - wasn't scored until the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

And now their unbeaten run in the WSL, which started all the way back on October 12 last year, has been ended by Chelsea.

It leaves the Gunners seven points adrift of leaders Man City already.

Head coach Renee Slegers was asked about that topic after full-time at Stamford Bridge and she said she wanted to "take the pressure off" of her players.

"I believe in these players. The goals will come and the points will come as well," she said.

"We have to earn the right again to talk about this [the title race] because we've lost too many points."

With a trip to City up next on October 4, the week ahead feels like a crucial one in the north Londoners' season.

Dan Long

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WSL match between Manchester United and West Ham United

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter highlighted Andrea Medina in the lead-up to this game, posing the question as to whether the Spaniard could be Man Utd's trump card.

Based on her performance on Sunday, the answer is a resounding yes.

Medina was the standout player by some distance at Leigh Sports Village: she created the most chances (4), took the most touches in the opposition box (11), hit the crossbar and scored United's crucial second goal.

Speaking on Sky Sports+, commentator Gary Taphouse called it "a virtuoso display". It came as no surprise when she was named Player of the Match.

As Eva Olid's side look to build momentum after starting with two defeats and a draw, the former Spain U23 international could be the keystone.

Dan Long

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WSL match between Liverpool and Everton

Liverpool's 2-0 win against Merseyside rivals Everton was the perfect remedy for the club's curse at Anfield.

Heading into this game, the Reds had lost eight of their last nine outings in the stadium. Five of those had come against the Toffees.

It was an assured and confident performance throughout. After Beata Olsson's early opener, which settled the nerves, it was just a matter of when, not if, the second arrived.

Cornelia Kapocs delivered and secured all three points. Liverpool move ahead of Everton in the process of their solid start to the campaign continuing.

The fixture list is a relentless one, however, with a trip to Birmingham in the Women's League Cup fast approaching before an away clash against another foe in Manchester United.

Getting over the hump that is their form at Anfield will be a welcome boost in tackling those challenges. Liverpool can now move forward with confidence.

Patrick Rowe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WSL match between Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa

A confident and strong 4-0 win for Tottenham against Aston Villa now opens up the conversation about a potential title race for the club.

No team has scored more than Spurs. Fifteen goals in their opening four games with just two goals conceded.

They are two points off Manchester City at the top but their upcoming run of fixtures will confirm whether they can assume the role of outside contenders for top spot.

London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal are their next three opponents in the WSL. Emerge from that October fixture list unscathed and serious conversations may need to be had about their chances...

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter said that people may need to start paying attention to Spurs in the build-up to this game. The game against Villa was another warning.

Patrick Rowe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WSL match between Birmingham City and Crystal Palace

Birmingham may still be waiting for their first WSL win of the season, but this was a display that shows it will not be far around the corner.

The Blues are playing in the top flight for the first time in four years but have started the season winless from their first four games.

Birmingham led twice against Palace on Sunday, yet somehow needed a late equaliser to rescue a 3-3 draw.

However, it was Birmingham who nearly nicked a winner as Chancelle Effa Effa had a stoppage-time chance to dramatically snatch victory.

That shot was one of 19 for the home side, who had more attempts, shots on target and touches in the opposition box than Palace.

But at the other end, they allowed 17 shots as two mistakes cost them two goals against Palace, as a goalkeeper howler let in the visitors' first while a slip gave Palace their third.

If Amy Merrick's side can tighten up at the back and continue to produce positive attacking displays like the one against Palace, then surely they can earn their first WSL win soon.

Declan Olley

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland put controversy aside to earn impressive win over Israel
Sports.content:
Football and politics are inseparable in the modern world, no matter how many people wish they were not. But whether the beautiful game can ease the ills of our age is another matter. After a week in which the issue of Irish support for the people of Gaza had turned this fixture into a battle of conscience, the outcome of this underwhelming match ultimately felt inconsequential.

In the end the result was indeed a walkover, just not because of a ­boycott. On Saturday night the ­question had been whether Heimir Hallgrimsson’s side would take to the field in Hungary at all. If they did, would their heads be in the game? It turned out that a week of internal angst had been enough to produce collective resolve among the Irish squad, or at least those selected to play. Strong and assertive from the off, their forwards each scored in the first half to settle the ­contest, with plenty of symbolic action to assure those back home of their feelings.

“It’s probably been the ­toughest days of my coaching career,” ­Hallgrimsson said after the match. “But it’s not about me. It’s about the players and they’ve shown today how much ­playing for Ireland means to them. They ­represented themselves on the pitch with dignity but also with the power of proud Irishmen. They’ve shown today how much playing for Ireland means to them and hopefully they will have the support of the Irish people.”

In a way the atmosphere in ­Debrecen was reminiscent of a match played during Covid. Every word uttered in the ground was audible and the nigh-on empty stands ­carried their own ­oppressive weight. As the nominal home side, Israel had been allowed a small delegation of fans, about 150, who were doing their best to be excitable. Meanwhile, two blocks away were the Irish ­contingent, around a dozen people who had got into the ground despite the Football Association of Ireland’s decision not to bring an away allocation. They were all stood hands in pockets in a stairway.

This odd, almost haunted mood was heightened further by Ireland’s mannered approach to the pre-match rituals. Irish staff faced away from the pitch when their national anthem was played. Ireland’s players, all wearing black armbands, stared at the ground during Israel’s. There was no exchanging of pennants and no shaking of hands, with both squads hurried away from the centre circle into their own huddles.

The game had come close to being abandoned on Saturday, when the goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu made ­himself unavailable for ­selection, his decision prompting ­emotional exchanges among players and ­management. Hallgrimsson ­therefore picked a team with defender Jimmy Dunne nominally a third goalkeeper and also dropped the key forward Finn Azaz to the bench in one of five changes to the team that lost meekly to Kosovo. Azaz’s mother has Israeli citizenship and the Southampton ­forward was reported to have made an impassioned contribution to Saturday’s discussion. “Today we thought others would fit this game better than him,” Halgrimsson said.

View image in fullscreen The Republic of Ireland team bow their heads during the Israeli national anthem. Photograph: Ben McShane/Sportsfile/Getty Images

After all the soul-searching, ­Ireland decided the contest in only 11 first-half minutes. Troy Parrott opened the scoring in the 14th ­minute, turning home a low shot through the body of Daniel Peretz after impressive work on the right by wingback James Abankwah. Two minutes later the lead was doubled when, running on the shoulder of the last defender, Adam Idah collected a smart through ball from Jack Moylan and wrapped a calm ­finish inside Peretz’s left-hand post.

In the 25th minute Moylan got a goal of his own, his fourth in as many caps to continue a stellar start to his international career, driving 25 yards into the box before shooting low into the net. Moylan wheeled away to the corner flag, took off his black ­armband and kissed it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Israel raised their levels ­momentarily in the second half, with the substitute Dor Peretz drawing one excellent save from Caoimhín ­Kelleher. But ultimately the game deteriorated into just a series of scuffles, cheered on deliriously by the Israeli support who appeared to be chanting for the IDF as the final whistle blew.

Their manager, Ran Ben-Shimon, was asked by Israeli media after the match if he would resign following the defeat, to which he answered no. “We didn’t handle the ­pressure well that is obvious, we failed ­mentally, we failed tactically,” Ben-Shimon said. “But in a few days there is another game we will have to find the energy to rise again.”

Sports.title: Tony Pulis says he and Stoke were ‘cheated’ in 2011 FA Cup final after Manchester City verdict
Sports.content:
Tony Pulis has said his Stoke City team were “cheated” out of the 2011 FA Cup after Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Pulis’s Stoke lost the 2011 Cup final 1-0 after Yaya Touré’s goal. Yet following Friday’s news that City are guilty on all but one of the more than 100 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, Pulis feels serious discontent. City are expected to appeal and they deny any wrongdoing.

“When do we get our FA Cup?” the 68-year-old wrote in his BBC Sport column. “That is what all Stoke fans have been asking me since the news broke on Friday. I thought exactly the same.

“I don’t expect Manchester City to offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners’ medals their players received. I don’t seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely.

“But I still feel cheated. We won’t ever get that day back and the chance to celebrate around Stoke-on-Trent with the cup and medals we so honestly fought for. After breaking the rules, Manchester City got to do that instead. While the process is far from over because City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth.”

Pulis pointed to City’s outlay on Touré, who was signed from Barcelona for £24m and earned about £180,000-a-week. He said: “Yaya Touré, who scored the winning goal, was reportedly earning 10 times what we were paying any of our players and, on his own, had cost more than our entire starting 11 when they had signed him from Barcelona in 2010.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester City’s Yaya Touré (left) scores during the 2011 FA Cup final. Photograph: Andrew Yates/AFP/Getty Images

Pulis underlined how his emotion has been changed by the verdict. “My disappointment was buried in the fact we had played a team full of superstars, and faced an elite coach in Roberto Mancini, and had just fallen short. Today, I feel very differently, as I am sure people connected with the other clubs affected by City’s successes in the same period, between 2009 and 2018 [will feel].

“We lost, but to a team that have been found guilty of breaking the financial rules set out by the Premier League. In doing so, they did not just beat Stoke in an FA Cup final, they collected a stack of titles and went on to completely dominate English football for more than a decade. So, with those rules having been broken, what will the punishment be?”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Tony Pulis of Stoke City reacts in defeat. Photograph: Laurence Griffiths/The FA/Getty Images

Pulis believes action may be widespread. “I know all Stoke supporters will be demanding that City pass the trophy over and every club that has been affected by their actions will be considering their legal options,” he said.

On Saturday, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, reiterated the club’s position. “There is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity,” said City’s chair.

On Friday a City spokesperson had said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023. The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel resists ‘madness’ of calls to rest England players despite longer window
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel says it would be “madness” to allow his England players or the clubs to pick and choose their matches during the elongated Nations League window as he promised to go full throttle for victory against Czechia in Prague on Tuesday.

The manager did accept that Declan Rice needed to rest and could not be part of the squad in light of the Arsenal midfielder’s heavy workload across a number of seasons and well-documented fitness issues. Rice was at Wembley on Saturday to watch England lose 3-2 against Spain in their opening Nations League game.

But now that Tuchel has his group, he says there is no room for compromise and certainly not to speak to club managers who might want to make deals over their players’ minutes. Tuchel does not want to rotate his starting personnel, although he does accept it could be impractical. After Prague, England go to Rijeka to play Croatia on Saturday before returning to Wembley to face Czechia next Tuesday.

“I don’t take calls from Premier League managers,” Tuchel said. “I never called any national team coach [when he was in club football]. I cannot manage [the minutes of] the players. It’s just impossible. I knew as a club coach … if I would call a coach in Brazil or Argentina, they would not know what I am talking about. The players would not know what I am talking about.

“Why would I do this and start giving the players the impression that it’s OK to take a step back or share a half or to rest one match? I would never. It’s madness. We want to win the next match. I would love not to rotate but I am not sure if it’s possible. An ideal scenario would be to go again and go again and go again. With six or seven players minimum that start again – to put the responsibility on them and for them to feel the trust.”

Tuchel accepted the Spain defeat had increased the pressure for the trip to Prague but he was unconcerned. “It’s nothing we can’t handle,” he said. “We need to be proactive and go for it. There is no room for managing [the players] or an economic style. It’s how the team want to play, how we want to play so let’s go.”

Tuchel was asked whether Jude Bellingham, who was at his rampaging best against Spain, could sustain his all-or-nothing style for another three England games in quick succession. “It’s the only style he can play,” Tuchel said.

“That’s just his game. It’s not an economic game. Let’s see. I would love to have him four times on the pitch. The concern is that he hasn’t done it this season in this tight period. We will need to check with the physios. We will not put Jude at any risk.”

Bellingham created a game-high five chances against Spain, including the assist for Anthony Gordon’s equaliser for 1-1. He won the penalty that Harry Kane missed that would have given England a 3-1 lead. His running with the ball repeatedly stretched the world champions. There was also the moment on 35 minutes when he clashed with his Real Madrid teammate Marc Cucurella.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane’s penalty miss was costly for England. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

“Jude likes that, he gets better if that happens,” Tuchel said. “It’s better if he plays with a bit of rage. It’s what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going. He doesn’t know any [Madrid] teammates [during an international game]. He is still friends with them but not for the 90 minutes.”

It was a wild game against Spain. England conceded early and could have been four or five down by the 35th minute. Their defending was loose. They rallied to lead 2-1 at half-time and the match turned after Kane’s penalty miss in the 54th minute when he felt his standing foot give way. Tuchel insisted his team was not far away from beating the very best.

“If Harry doesn’t slip we win the game,” Tuchel said. “If Harry doesn’t slip we go two goals up. We were clearly the better team until that moment. Of course, Spain never panic. How far away are we from that? One small slip from Harry.

“If we had won, we would have deserved it but it wouldn’t have made us favourites for the Euros. We need to go step by step. They came with their strongest team. We had some key players missing. I am fine with this performance. We could have won the game and didn’t.”

Sports.title: Nations League: Greece stun Klopp’s Germany, Netherlands sink Serbia but Gakpo hurt
Sports.content:
Greece stunned Germany 1-0 in Augsburg to go top of their Nations League group and spoil Jürgen Klopp’s debut in the home dugout.

Dimitrios Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany. Ivan Jovanovic’s side now lead ⁠Group A2 with six points ⁠from two matches; Klopp’s side are third with one point from two games after a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands on Thursday.

The hosts were in control for most of the game and had close to 80% possession in the first half alone. Germany were ultimately punished ⁠for sloppy defending, especially in the second half, which gave the visitors space to attack.

Felix Nmecha fired wide in the 54th minute, moments after the Greece keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis ‌had palmed a Joshua Kimmich free-kick over the bar. The Greeks then almost scored in the 66th after Kimmich lost possession in his own half, but the substitute Fotis Ioannidis fired just wide of the post.

View image in fullscreen It was a frustrating first home game in charge of the Germany side for Jürgen Klopp. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

They did better eight minutes later, with Kourbelis’s deflected low drive earning their second victory in a row after their last-gasp 2-1 win over Serbia on Thursday. Greece will now host the Dutch on Thursday, while Germany are at home to Serbia.

Klopp shrugged off the defeat after the final whistle. “Personally, I’m completely unbothered by it,” he told ARD. “I’ve lost far more matches in my life than I would have liked … but as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately just a piece of information – no different from a win.”

“We absolutely need these kinds of matches – they are exactly the games we wanted to have,” Klopp added, while Kimmich said his new coach “has been very clear about what he wants – as players, we need to implement it”.

Earlier, the Netherlands earned a 2-1 victory in Serbia thanks to Mexx ‌Meerdink’s double on his second appearance for his country. It was their first win under their new coach, Xavi Hernández, following Thursday’s draw with Germany.

Meerdink, who plays for the Eredivisie leaders, AZ, opened the scoring with a confidently taken penalty in the 30th minute. Luka Jovic equalised for the hosts but Meerdink struck again in the 69th minute to earn three points.

“It’s a boyhood dream,” Meerdink said. “Everything is happening so quickly. You just don’t realise what can happen in the space of a week. It’s also great that we managed to win here. I did feel a little pressure, but you play that out of your system. And then to score two ​is fantastic.”

Cody Gakpo is an injury concern after going off in the 17th minute and will undergo a scan on Monday. “It’s his ankle, that’s all I know,” Xavi said on the Liverpool winger’s injury. “Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it’s not too important.”

View image in fullscreen Mexx Meerdink scores his second goal in the Netherlands’ 2-1 victory in Belgrade. Photograph: Marko Đurica/Reuters

João Félix scored for the second ​consecutive Portugal match as the defending champions edged past Norway 2-1 in Oslo to top Group A4 with two wins from two games. Erling Haaland cancelled out João Félix’s 17th-minute opener in the 54th minute, but Gonçalo ​Ramos’s chip three minutes later secured victory for Jorge Jesus’s side in Oslo.

Bruno Fernandes was left out of the Portugal squad on Sunday, with Jesus revealing beforehand that the Manchester United captain had “played through the pain” in Thursday’s 1-0 win over Wales.

“He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United,” the Portugal head coach said. “He wasn’t his usual self … [but] he really wanted to play against Wales.”

Portugal stay in Scandinavia for their next game, away to Denmark on Thursday. Norway visit Cardiff to take on Wales, who earlier lost 2-0 to the Danes in Copenhagen.

Sports.title: McTominay’s role a poser for Pocognoli as Scotland offer positives in Slovenia
Sports.content:
An elongated international window does not prevent Sébastien Pocognoli from glancing towards the next one. Scott McTominay’s absence from Scotland’s opening set of Nations League games is understandable as the Napoli midfielder recovers from a heart procedure.

The scoreless draw in Slovenia on Saturday raised the question of where McTominay will fit in when he returns. “He can play in many positions,” Pocognoli said. “He is a top player so he can read the game. We will see.”

Indeed we will. The answer is not immediately obvious. Pocognoli deployed Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson as central midfielders in Ljubljana with John McGinn placed ahead of them to support a two-man strike force. Gilmour was heavily influential during Scotland’s impressive second half. Ferguson’s combative and defensive skills are valuable. McGinn, like McTominay, is a mainstay of the team. It is therefore legitimate to ask how Pocognoli handles McTominay, who is expected to return to the Scotland scene in November.

“For now we just need to put the structure in place,” Pocognoli said. “I hope Scott watched the game and thought ‘OK, I see myself in that shape in the second half’, and that with good discipline he can enjoy it. I hope he can look and think: ‘Yeah, I want to play.’

“Andy Robertson was really positive after the game and said that he really enjoyed it. It is really good to hear that from top players.”

That Scotland improved markedly after half-time messaging from Pocognoli, in his maiden match as the country’s manager, reflected well on the 39‑year‑old Belgian. Pocognoli seems determined to emphasise that he is not tactically inflexible, despite Scotland’s shape being typical of what he deployed at Union Saint‑Gilloise and Monaco. Pocognoli also insisted there will be consistent involvement for Ben Gannon-Doak, a winger who does not automatically seem to fit into a 3-4-1-2 setup. Gannon‑Doak, whose game time has been restricted at Bournemouth, appeared as a second-half substitute in Slovenia.

“It will not be difficult to find a place for him,” Pocognoli said. “It is a process. At his club he also needs to settle. He is young and he needs to play more for his club.

“He is a top, top kid first of all and a top player and a gamechanger and we don’t have a lot of those. That is why Josh McPake is also with us because I want more of that. Maybe in the future if those two make the step we can be open to exploring many shapes.

“I think in that wide position in the shape we had in Slovenia it is risky to start him, because we have to know that sometimes you can be beaten in transition. The pattern on the ball can sometimes be bad and then it is not the game for Ben. But when we have good control on the pitch, like in the second half, that becomes his game.”

View image in fullscreen Sébastien Pocognoli is in a tricky position of trying to learn about his team while facing credible opposition. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

A sterner test surely awaits for Scotland on Tuesday. Switzerland may be without Granit Xhaka but they still swatted aside North Macedonia 3-0 on Saturday evening. Pocognoli is in that tricky position of trying to learn about his squad while facing credible opposition. He was aware of the frustrations of the Scotland support during the first half in Slovenia, with those fans roused by the creation of numerous second‑half chances.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“As long as we continue to create chances, you bring the fans alive,” Pocognoli said. “If we can produce the second-half performance at home I think it will be OK. But we cannot play 90 minutes like this. When we are resilient like we were in defending the box in the first half that is something we have to enjoy because it is not easy to defend like they did.

“I think the crowd was positive at the end because we produced something that they wanted to see. At least we attacked and they did not have the feeling that they travelled for nothing.”

Oli McBurnie is likely to retain his place in attack despite his run without scoring in Scotland colours stretching to 17 games. Pocognoli has been delighted with the application and attitude of McBurnie, who had been shunned by the previous manager, Steve Clarke. Scotland need potency; they have found the net only once in four games.

“He played a good game,” Pocognoli said of McBurnie. “In the first half when it was difficult … but in that moment you give up or you stick together to fight for the team. Oli never gave up. He showed that he is proud and hungry to be here.”

Sports.title: Chelsea turn up heat on Arsenal as Alyssa Thompson strike settles WSL derby
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s title chances were dealt a significant blow after a narrow defeat at the hands of Chelsea. Alyssa Thompson’s first-half finish was the difference on a competitive afternoon at Stamford Bridge but one that ultimately left Renée Slegers with more questions than answers about how to save their season.

“Worried? No,” Slegers said. “Confidence is something that fluctuates. They know who they are and they know what they can bring. What’s important is that there’s always phases in the season and there’s different things you need to work on or focus on.

“It’s important that we keep any pressure and any complexity away from the players because we believe in them. It’s just really important that we keep that simplicity and clear minds for the players.”

There is no game quite as eagerly anticipated in the Women’s Super League as the meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal. While other derbies and duels are in their early development, the London derby is the one year after year that brings the pressure, the drama and, of course, the eyeballs. While both sides clearly respect each other off the pitch, there is a distinct sense that once they cross the white line there is true competitive animosity there, one that lifts the levels of everyone in the vicinity.

This edition was no different with expectation and apprehension buzzing around Stamford Bridge before kick-off and no shortage of new narratives. This was the first time Katie McCabe, 11 years a Gunner, would face her old team having moved in the summer. Would she help Chelsea to inflict more pain on Arsenal’s stuttering start, or could Slegers’s side put a pin in the pressure balloon and breathe new life into their search for a first title in eight years?

Both teams came into this encounter having not yet hit form. Arsenal have created opportunities but have looked predictable in their buildup and lacked a finishing touch. In contrast, Chelsea have looked energetic and full of ideas but, excluding their win against Manchester United, have also struggled with ruthlessness in front of goal.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Katie McCabe took on her former Arsenal teammates for the first time since her summer move. Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Sonia Bompastor was handed a significant boost before kick-off with the news that both Keira Walsh and Lauren James were available to start. Lexi Potter was given the nod alongside Walsh in midfield, a sign of how much trust the head coach has in the 20-year-old, while Melvine Malard was fit enough to begin up front.

Slegers, meanwhile, rang the changes from Arsenal’s hard-fought victory against HB Køge during the week. Two who remained were Kyra Cooney-Cross and the goalkeeper Anneke Borbe, who kept out Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors came out full of energy and looking to make an early statement. They dominated early on with 44.2% of the action happening in Chelsea’s defensive third in the first quarter and Arsenal looking to reap the rewards of their high press.

Their biggest threat early on came from Lisa Baum. The 19-year-old has been one of the more positive aspects of their season to date and was given space down the right by Chelsea.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

For all of their control, however, it was much of the same old story for Slegers’s side, haunted by their inability to take their chances. Of the eight shots they created, they failed to register one on target and hit the woodwork twice through Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey.

With every rattle of a post that reverberated around Stamford Bridge, Arsenal’s early confidence dwindled and Bompastor’s side started to find more joy. In direct contrast to their opponents, the Blues took their chance when it came when Malard pounced on Steph Catley as she played out from the back. Borbe made a good save to deny Walsh initially but the rebound fell perfectly for Thompson to hammer home.

It was the ideal time to score and Chelsea went in ahead at the break with the momentum of the game having shifted significantly. They went on to create big opportunities of their own with Malard dragging a shot narrowly wide on two occasions.

While Arsenal were able to create opportunities, the hosts looked comfortable in the circumstances and defended resolutely to see out the game and take home a valuable three points.

Sports.title: Denmark dominate Wales in Nations League to leave Bellamy ‘really hurting’
Sports.content:
Wales wilted in Copenhagen as a 2-0 defeat to Denmark left them bottom of their Nations League group with no points or goals from their first two games.

After a first half in which Wales were very much second-best and fortunate to reach the break level, Denmark’s domination was rewarded by a Ben Davies own goal and a Gustav Isaksen strike in the second period.

Wales lost Thursday’s opener to Portugal 1-0 and Sunday’s result leaves them already facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation from Group A4. Denmark were under similar pressure after being beaten 3-2 by Norway on Thursday, but rose to the occasion and should have won more comfortably.

“I’m really hurting. When you see an athletic team run over you a little bit … but then, will we improve? I think we will,” said the Wales manager, Craig Bellamy. “This team will get better, these players will keep improving. For me now it’s just focus, two more games to go.”

Bellamy had happy memories of the Parken Stadium when as a 19-year-old he had scored the Wales winner in a Euro 2000 qualifier. Bellamy had promised to make changes given the short turnaround of fixtures and, in the event, made six with Charlie Savage’s surprise promotion the most notable switch.

The son of former Wales international Robbie Savage, Charlie joined the squad after several withdrawals, with his previous two caps having both come against Gibraltar. Daniel James, Kieffer Moore and Sorba Thomas formed a reshaped frontline, while Chris Mepham and Connor Roberts were drafted into defence.

View image in fullscreen Craig Bellamy made a number of changes to the team that lost 1-0 in Portugal, but could not deliver a different result. Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Denmark were soon playing their way through a porous Wales midfield though, and chances came their way. Neco Williams was caught out by Joachim Andersen’s pass from the back and Isaksen flashed his shot wide. Isaksen then sent over a cross that Patrick Dorgu headed off target.

The hosts thought they had taken the lead after 24 minutes. Wales were exposed by a counterattack led by Mikkel Damsgaard and Isaksen met Rasmus Højlund’s cross with a thumping volley, only for VAR to rule offside in the buildup.

Damsgaard struck a post seconds later and it looked a matter of time before Denmark would score. But Dorgu headed off straight down the tunnel in a potential injury blow for Manchester United, and Wales began to create chances of their own.

Thomas was just off target from 20 yards after an Andersen error and Wales went even closer two minutes before the interval. Brennan Johnson got to the byline after working a one-two with Thomas and pulled the ball back to Roberts, whose shot under pressure was tipped away by Filip Jörgensen from close range.

Williams fired straight at Jörgensen at the start of the second half, but Wales were behind after 53 minutes from a free-kick. Damsgaard delivered a delicious ball and, while Højlund wheeled away celebrating the final touch, it ultimately went in off the unfortunate Davies for an own goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Isaksen put the contest beyond Wales after 66 minutes. Moore headed off the Wales goalline, but the Lazio winger was quickest on to the loose ball and his deflected strike went in off the underside of the bar.

Mohamed Daramy spurned a great chance to add further Danish gloss and both sides had late efforts ruled out, with Williams’s header disallowed for a push by Ethan Ampadu.

It does not get any easier for Wales with a visit from Erling Haaland’s Norway on Thursday, before a return date against Denmark in Cardiff.

“I said to the players before the game, ‘this is going to be tougher than Portugal’,” Bellamy added. “It was a different challenge, but a very difficult one. The best team won overall.

“As disappointed as I am with that, the result I probably think was fair. We move on. It will be a tough watch back. How the players put their bodies on the line was brilliant. They are really special for that. I really admire that, but I want more.”

Sports.title: Liverpool sink Everton and end derby drought after Olsson and Kapocs strike
Sports.content:
At last, their wait is over. Liverpool’s players could gather in front of the Kop for a celebratory team photograph after the final whistle and rejoice in a new feeling, after beating Everton at Anfield in a Women’s Super League fixture for the first time and finally ending their long run of derby pain.

After six wins from six visits to Anfield for Everton in the WSL era and even quips from their former manager Brian Sørensen in previous campaigns about making Anfield their “training pitch” during their persistent run of victories in this showpiece fixture, Beata Olsson’s early header and Cornelia Kapocs’s late finish were enough to give them a deserved 2-0 victory.

“It’s nice to break that duck, definitely,” the Liverpool head coach, Gareth Taylor, said. “We just downplayed the game, if that makes sense, because it becomes something that’s so big that players start to worry. We want players to go out and feel natural, like they’re playing like they were when they were growing up.

“It is nice because it’s a stat that can just grow and grow. I felt we were hard done by [at Anfield] last season – if you look at their xG in that game, they scored four goals but they were absolute worldies, whereas today we’ve scored two [but] we probably could have had six.”

Taylor was not wrong; the hosts were undeniably the better side and should have scored more goals. Indeed, they would have done had it not been for the heroics of the Everton midfielder Ruby Mace.

When Olsson got in front of her marker, Hannah Blundell, to meet Natalia Ramos’s right-sided corner and angle her header perfectly, diagonally across goal and into the far corner inside the first four minutes you could have been forgiven for thinking Liverpool were set for an easy afternoon such was the simplicity of the goal. Instead, what followed was something of a slog at times with Liverpool trying to break down an Everton backline that initially proved difficult to open up.

After the break, another set piece almost did the job for Liverpool but Vivien Endemann’s volley smacked against the crossbar. By now the pressure was almost relentless and, with just over 20 minutes remaining, Ramos looked certain to score, with time to shoot less than 10 yards out. But the effort was blocked by Mace, who threw her body in front of the ball to keep her side in the contest.

Five minutes later, Mace again came to Everton’s rescue and hooked Kapocs’s effort off the line. The Liverpool forward’s attempted header had come off the top of her shoulder and bounced goalwards, but Mace intervened just in time.

View image in fullscreen Cornelia Kapocs fires in Liverpool’s second goal against Everton. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Eventually, Kapocs found room inside the area to turn and fire home in the closing stages, much to the relief of Liverpool’s supporters. The result continued the side’s encouraging start to the campaign as they moved on to seven points from their opening four games, their only defeat having come away against the defending champions, Manchester City.

It took Taylor’s side until 25 January to accumulate seven points last season but they look significantly improved and have built on the progress they made during the second half of 2025-26.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors had spurned a couple of decent chances on the counterattack before the break, including Hannah Cain scuffing over from a promising position. Overall, however, Everton, whose only two league goals this season have been own goals, will be concerned about their comparative lack of creativity.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Spurs go second, Man Utd earn first win Show Victoria Pelova scored twice as Tottenham moved up to second in the WSL table with a 4-0 win over Aston Villa, while Manchester United earned their first win of the season, edging West Ham 2-1. Dutch midfielder Pelova [pictured] broke the deadlock in the 54th minute at Brisbane Road, and then fired in a second off the underside of the crossbar, taking her tally to four goals in two WSL games. Spurs sealed victory as Caitlin Dijkstra headed in, and Cathinka Tandberg added a fourth with two minutes left. Manchester United secured their first WSL victory under new manager Eva Olid, defeating West Ham in Leigh. Elisabeth Terland’s header set United on their way after nine minutes, with summer signing Andrea Medina doubling the lead late in the second half. Viviane Asseyi scored a late penalty for the visitors. Océane Hurtré fired Birmingham City ahead after 40 seconds against Crystal Palace, scoring the quickest goal of the season so far. Shanade Hopcroft’s long-range free-kick had Palace level on the half-hour, before Hurtré restored Birmingham’s lead with an angled strike. Palace fought back to lead at St Andrew's, their goals coming from Bethany England and Lexi Lloyd-Smith, but Suzu Amano struck with three minutes left to secure Birmingham a point in a thrilling 3-3 draw. Press Assocation Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Asked about that wait for one of his own players to score a league goal, the Everton head coach, Scott Phelan, spoke calmly, saying: “We know we need to be more decisive in those actions, 100%. We have won two games as well and three on the bounce, so we don’t forget that. [But] yes, we want to start contributing more in the final third and that’ll be a challenge for all of us.

“We’ve played four games, so it’s definitely not panic stations. We’ve got good players in those areas of the pitch, we’re convinced they will contribute more – we’ve just got to wait for that moment to appear and hopefully it’s sooner rather than later.”

Phelan’s team still sit comfortably in the middle of the table with two wins from four games. Perhaps the most disappointing aspect for Everton fans will be that they can no longer rely on their annual collection of three points from Anfield.

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini breaks silence on Manchester City guilty verdict: Club's former manager - accused of receiving 'double' contract from owners - insists it's 'not my problem'
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has claimed Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules is 'not my problem', despite the club's failure to disclose his full pay being among the alleged breaches. The Premier League accused the club of widespread financial doping over an era of sustained success and Daily Mail Sport understands they have succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims. City have won 26 trophies since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, including eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups and the Champions League as part of their 2023 Treble-winning season. Among the alleged breaches by the club was an alleged failure to provide full details of Mancini's pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13. In 2018, German publication Der Spiegel dropped a series of bombshell articles based on a tranche of emails obtained by subsequently convicted Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto. It was claimed Manchester City had been effectively cheating by using a variety of underhand techniques to swerve both Premier League and UEFA rules on financial fair play. Roberto Mancini has claimed Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules is 'not my problem' Der Spiegel alleged in 2018 that Mancini received a separate payment for four days' work as a consultant on top of his Man City salary after being appointed the club's manager in 2009 Mancini, it was alleged, had signed a £1.45million a year deal with the club when he took over as City manager in 2009 but had also picked up £1.75million a year for four days' work as a consultant for Abu Dhabi side Al Jazira, which is also owned by Man City owner Sheikh Mansour. The 61-year-old, who began his second spell as Italy boss earlier this week, defended Man City after being asked about the verdict while insisting the case was 'not my problem'. 'I don't think Manchester City were found guilty, on the contrary,' Mancini said, as per Gazzetta Dello Sport. 'It's not a problem that concerns me, but it's not a new thing. 'Manchester City are not guilty and the double contract is not my problem, but theirs if anything.' During his time at Man City, Mancini led the club to victory in the 2011 FA Cup, representing their first major trophy since 1976. Tony Pulis, who managed beaten finalists Stoke City, has claimed he feels 'cheated' following the verdict in the Man City case. Mancini famously then led Man City to the Premier League title in the 2011-12 season, which was clinched by Sergio Aguero's injury time winner. Mancini famously led Man City to the Premier League title in 2012, which was clinched by Sergio Aguero's injury time winning goal against QPR Rio Ferdinand and David de Gea, who were part of the Man United side that dramatically finished second, have both called for Man City to be stripped of that title in recent days. Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024. Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges. The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period. The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18. As well as allegedly failing to provide full details of Mancini's pay, Man City were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023. Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups. On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’. In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.' In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began. ‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies. ‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: The new Miracle at Medinah: Team USA completes wild comeback to win the Presidents Cup in front of Trump
Sports.content:
The new Miracle at Medinah: Team USA completes wild comeback to win the Presidents Cup in front of Trump

Team USA completed one of the greatest comebacks in Presidents Cup history to overcome their international rivals in front of a raucous crowd at Medinah.

The Americans headed into Sunday singles three points down and at risk of a humbling loss, but Scottie Scheffler and Co won eight of the 12 singles matches to seal an 11th straight win.

The day began with a rousing speech from Donald Trump, before the players went out and stormed back, with Jacob Bridgeman clinching the trophy for his country.

There were key rallies on the back nine by two-time major champion Collin Morikawa and 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun.

Outplayed over three days in team matches, the Americans leaned on their strength in singles to make up a three-point deficit.

President Trump was on the first tee for the start of all 12 singles matches, and he kept his speech short. 'It's going to be a very interesting game of golf,' he said.

Team USA celebrates after Jackson Koivun secured a huge win for his country at Medinah

Jacob Bridgeman holed the winning putt as America surged back from three points down

The day began with a speech from Donald Trump, who watched the start of all 12 matches

The president had hot-footed it to Illinois fresh from watching Texas beat Tennessee in Knoxville on Saturday, and he drew roaring applause from the packed grandstands at Medinah.

Dressed in a dark suit and red tie, Trump smiled, pumped his fists, and blew kisses to the excited crowd as spectators broke out into deafening chants of 'USA! USA!'

Taking to the microphone ahead of the Sunday singles matches, Trump poked fun at reports that he had requested a 15-minute speech window from the PGA Tour.

'You know, the fake news media will say I got a very bad reception. We got a good reception!' Trump told the cheering gallery.

'He [PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp] said, could you make a short speech? I said, no, I don't have the courage to make a speech - these people want to see golf, they don't want to hear speeches!

''I'll only say this: Our country is doing great, better than ever before.'

His Sunday arrival brought enhanced security measures across Medinah, with gates opening at 8 a.m. as the Secret Service implemented tight restrictions.

Koivun celebrates after birdieing the 12th hole on his way to a big win in the Sunday singles

Trump continued his whirlwind weekend of sport on Sunday after attending the Texas game

The lighthearted quip came after Golfweek reported on Saturday that Trump had asked organizers for 15 minutes to address the crowd before the start of play.

Trump stepped aside quickly to let the action begin, as Brandt Snedeker's U.S. squad looked to battle back from a 10.5 - 7.5 deficit against Geoff Ogilvy's International team.

On Sunday, it was Cameron Young and Justin Thomas who set the tone early. Scottie Scheffler took down Nico Echavarria with a show of pure sportsmanship when a spectator disrupted the Colombian's swing.

Patrick Cantlay had another moment, as he always seem to do in this competition, holing a birdie putt from just inside 60 feet on the par-3 16th against hard-luck Adam Scott.

Scottie Scheffler was another of the Americans who secured a big win at Medinah on Sunday

Trump is accompanied by Secret Service as he walks to make his speech at the Presidents Cup

Outside the gates at Medinah, some anti-Trump protestors spoke out against the president

Five matches remained on the course - the Americans were 1 up in three of them, the other two were all square. All the Internationals had to do was find three points from them. The Americans simply refused to budge.

Koivun was 2 down through 10 holes to the Internationals' top performer this week, Si Woo Kim, when he won three straight holes to flip the color to American red on the board. The kid drilled his tee shot on the 18th, and twirled his iron when he knew the approach was pure. He wound up with a 2-up victory, and then it was a matter of time.

The clinching point came from Jacob Bridgeman, who rolled in a 3-foot par putt on the 18th green for a 1-up victory over Min Woo Lee, assuring the Americans the 15 1/2 points they needed.

Sports.title: Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'
Sports.content:
Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'

Manchester City's former chairman David Bernstein believes punishment handed to the club after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules must affect their top flight status.

Daily Mail Sport reported that the Premier League has succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims against Man City, with the club found guilty of the 'vast majority' of the 115 charges of financial rule breaking.

An appeal from Man City is considered an inevitability, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak declaring on Saturday that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as Football Association chair 2011-13, has warned that financial penalties will not be enough of a punishment.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Bernstein stressed the fines would not be sufficient as he cited their vast spending in the previous transfer window.

Man City spent £440million in the summer and equalled the British transfer record signing £125million Enzo Fernandez.

Man City's former chairman David Bernstein believes the club's Premier League status is at risk after they were found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 rule break charges

Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as FA chair 2011-13

Bernstein believes that while the club's wealth would render a fine insufficient, Man City could face automatic relegation or a points deduction that effectively ensures they will drop out of the top flight.

'I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough,' Bernstein said.

'We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient.

'Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status.

'And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing.

'Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down.

'But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know.

'I think it does depend partly on the timing.'

Bernstien suggested Man City's wealth would make a financial penalty for the club 'insufficient'

Man City enjoyed staggering success during the years covered by the Premier League charges

Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that the verdict will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800million.

In late 2024, Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight – be found guilty.

Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City’s cheating.

On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak insisted the club remains confident of clearing their name and ‘proving innocence’

In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp's home debut falls flat as Germany suffer surprise defeat by Greece - as former captain tears into 'average' team
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp suffered defeat in his first home match as Germany boss as Greece earned a shock 1-0 victory in their Nations League match. Dimitrios Kourbelis struck 16 minutes from time in Augsburg to give Greece, who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups, a famous win. Kourbelis's deflected effort ensured Greece beat Germany in an international match for the first time. Klopp is yet to win either of his first two games in charge of Germany after his team were held to a 1-1 draw by the Netherlands on his return to the dugout on Thursday. The former Liverpool boss took the job after leaving his role as global director of football at the Red Bull group. 'The result isn't great, but it's part of the process, absolutely,' Klopp told ARD. Jurgen Klopp suffered defeat in his first home match as Germany boss as Greece earned a shock 1-0 victory Dimitrios Kourbelis scored the winner for Greece, who beat Germany for the first time 'The line-up, the way the team was put together, and all the changes were 100 per cent my responsibility. That was my idea. 'It was clear that we weren’t going to completely tear apart a deep-sitting opponent. I could have easily lived with not winning the game by a big margin, but you can’t lose it. 'The goal was unlucky, but it fits in a way with the situations they had. They were basically just playing long balls. We defended those first balls reasonably well in most situations, but we weren’t as dominant as we could have been given the physical quality of our players. 'We've only been together for a week, we're a newly formed team, so we need routines. Football needs training. Everything was great this week, except for large parts of this game.' Klopp added: 'There's no reason for me to fall into depression and say: "we're so bad". We're not. But we're also not that good. 'I don't want the players to be judged conclusively: this one can't do this or that. If you want to criticise someone, do it with me. 'Let the new ones develop. The established ones, they're top players in their clubs, they have my support. And feel free to criticise me, but not the boys. 'I was surprised that some people booed. The future is as rosy as we imagine it. We're going at it with everything we've got. We'll continue down the path.' Klopp defended his players post-match and volunteered to take the criticism for the defeat Former Germany captain Bastian Schweinsteiger tore into the team after the defeat, the country's first against the Euro 2004 winners. 'We're no longer a top team,' said Schweinsteiger. 'We're now just an average team. 'We no longer have players who make the difference. Even Greece have Karetsas, Tzolis, Pavlidis - for me those are players who make the difference. 'Hopefully Jürgen Klopp manages to develop a team that can play Klopp football.' Klopp had warned his side pre-match that they were facing Greece's 'golden generation'. The Germany boss will have a new squad for their next two Nations League fixtures of the international break. It followed him calling up 44 players earlier this month, with the former Liverpool boss splitting the group into two to handle the fixtures and give him an opportunity to assess more players. Germany lie third in their Nations League group on one point, with Greece leading the way on six and the Netherlands lying in second on four. Klopp will seek a first victory when Germany host Serbia on October 1, before taking on Greece again three days later.

Sports.title: Ireland stars REFUSE to shake hands of Israeli opponents and bow their heads during national anthem ahead of controversial clash after goalkeeper withdrew from squad in protest at 'atrocities in Gaza'
Sports.content:
Ireland's players bowed their heads during the Israel national anthem and did not shake hands with their opponents before the controversial Nations League clash in Hungary. The fixture has been shrouded in controversy after the Irish team and officials came under huge pressure to stage a boycott due to Israel’s military actions in Gaza. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad, with the Bolton star saying ‘I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle’. 'My decision is based purely upon my belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong,' he addded. 'It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition to the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region.' Players voted to fulfil the fixture and also agreed to wear black armbands in recognition of all the lives lost in the conflict. Ireland also decided against giving a pennant to Israel to mark the match - a standard gesture in all international fixtures. The customary pre-match handshake did not take place and during the playing of the Israel anthem, Ireland's starting XI looked towards the floor in unison - as did their substitutes. The Ireland XI look to the floor during the playing of the Israel national anthem Israel's players stood for the anthem as Ireland's bowed their heads The Irish side did stand proud for their own national anthem Ireland's substitutes and staff also looked at the floor during Israel's anthem, with the squad having voted to play the match Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad due to Israel's actions in Gaza Heimir Hallgrimsson was heavily criticised in Israel for saying Ireland are 'playing against genocide' Ireland won 3-0 after first-half goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan, who took off his black armband and kissed it when celebrating. There were no handshakes as full time and Ireland’s players were booed as they left the field. Manager Heimir Hallgrimsson had also said that ‘nobody is comfortable playing these games for many reasons’ and, earlier in the week, said his team were ‘playing against genocide’. A training session on Saturday was delayed by five hours after players decided whether to boycott the match which was held in Debrecen, Hungary, with Israel playing in neutral venues due to the conflict. FAI chief executive David Courell said a ‘significant majority’ voted to play. UEFA rules mean teams must name at least three goalkeepers in their squad and Bazunu's withdrawal meant that Jimmy Dunne, the QPR centre back, was named as a keeper on the official team-sheet. Irish broadcaster RTE cut back its screening of the game with no studio punditry, no advertising and only using commentary from an international feed. Many pubs in Ireland refused to show the game and there were protests outside the team hotel in Dublin earlier in the week. Ireland are set to play Israel again on Sunday but it will be behind closed doors at a neutral venue in Serbia.
